newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia mulling new incentives for oil investors.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia mulling new incentives for oil investors.

text.p: Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Thursday the government will consider offering new incentives to oil investors in an effort to boost exploration but added tax laws could not be relaxed.
"We evaluate our rules every time so all parties can benefit," Sudjana told reporters after state oil company Pertamina signed eight production sharing contracts with foreign firms.
"Certainly oil investors hope for facilities and incentives that are of benefit for them," he said. "We always accomodate their demands except for tax. We have a law on tax."
"Therefore, Pertamina will negotiate with the oil investors on what their demands are and we will see," Sudjana said.
Foreign oil contractors in Indonesia have said they need incentives, especially tax breaks, to encourage exploration for new oil fields.
"We cannot give the tax breaks, but we can consider other incentives. It depends on their (oil investors') demands," Sudjana said. He gave no details.
Pertamina's contracts included one with a unit of Canada's Carmanah Resources Ltd, a Pertamina spokesman said.
Under the contract, GFB Resources Indonesia, a wholly owned unit of Carmanah, will invest $96 million to explore a block offshore North East Natuna, in the South China Sea, the spokesman said.

Pertamina also signed production sharing contracts with Japan Petroleum Exploration Co (JAPEX), Indonesia Petroleum Ltd (INPEX), both of Japan, Apache Corp of the United States and units of Australia's City View Corp, New Zealand's Cue Energy Resources unit and Total of France.
